beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards down. "Let's see the whole run-up to this."

beats.prompt: The past: the commission where you learned the tools were already enough.
The present: the read you trusted before you could explain it.
The future: the bigger contract you're about to pull off together.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Quiz me — if the Chariot's about a strong start, does that mean the hard part's basically over once we begin?"

options.text: No — it's the initiating push, not the whole journey.
Yes, everything after the start takes care of itself.
The Chariot has nothing to do with how long this takes.

elaboration: The Chariot's energy is for getting the cart moving — it doesn't promise anything about sustaining that pace once you're rolling.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "And if he and I disagree again three weeks in, does that mean the two horses were never actually aligned?"

options.text: No — aligning them isn't a one-time fix, it's ongoing work.
Yes, that means the whole partnership was doomed from day one.
Disagreement means one of you should quit.

elaboration: Two horses don't get aligned once and stay that way forever — the Chariot's job is steering them back together every time they start to pull apart.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: what you already had, the read you trusted, and the push you're only now making together."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think I've been expecting the alignment to be permanent instead of something we keep doing. That's actually useful to hear before Monday."
